keys.Description: An SSH server package or unit exists on the host.
The SSH service is running or socket-activated.
UnitFileState of the first present SSH unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
An SSH unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
A telnet server package, unit or inetd entry exists on the host.
The telnet service is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present telnet unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A telnet unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
A telnet server would accept a connection from off the host (active unit or listening socket unit, non-loopback).
A finger server package, unit or inetd entry exists on the host.
The finger service is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present finger unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A finger unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
A finger server would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).
An r-services server (rsh/rlogin/rexec) unit or inetd entry exists on the host.
An r-services daemon is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present r-services unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
An r-services unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
An r-services daemon would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).

A simple TCP/IP service is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present simple-service unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A simple TCP/IP service unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
A simple TCP/IP service would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).

The NFS server is running or reachable on its port.

An NFS server unit will start at boot.

The autofs service is running.

An autofs unit will start at boot.
An rpcbind unit exists on the host.

UnitFileState of the first present rpcbind unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
An rpcbind unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
The rpcbind service would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).
An NIS (ypserv/ypbind) unit exists on the host.
An NIS daemon is running.
UnitFileState of the first present NIS unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
An NIS unit will start at boot.
A TFTP server unit or inetd entry exists on the host.
The TFTP service is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present TFTP unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A TFTP unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
The TFTP service would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).

The talk service is running, socket-activated or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present talk unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A talk unit will start at boot or on socket activation.
The talk service would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).
An SNMP daemon unit exists on the host.
The SNMP service is running or reachable on its port.
UnitFileState of the first present SNMP unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
An SNMP unit will start at boot.
The SNMP service would accept a connection from off the host (non-loopback listener).
A time-synchronisation daemon unit (chrony, systemd-timesyncd, ntpd or ntpsec) exists on the host.
A time-synchronisation daemon is running.
UnitFileState of the first present time-synchronisation unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A time-synchronisation unit will start at boot.
A syslog daemon unit (rsyslog or syslog-ng) exists on the host.
The syslog daemon is running.
UnitFileState of the first present syslog unit (evidence only; "not-found" when none).
A syslog unit will start at boot.
Listening TCP/UDP sockets with proto, address, port, inode, pid and executable.
How sshd options were obtained - G, T or parse.
Whether per-persona (Match) values were collected; false means options hold global values only.
Effective PermitRootLogin value (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
OpenSSH version reported by sshd -V (major.minor); absent when it could not be read.
Effective MaxAuthTries (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
Effective ClientAliveInterval in seconds (daemon-reported versus parsed files); 0 disables the keepalive.
Effective ClientAliveCountMax (daemon-reported versus parsed files).
Effective Banner path, or none for sshd's default of no pre-auth banner.
Every Include the sshd_config parse followed, in expansion order - path, line, depth.
Whether the file named by sshd's Banner exists; false when Banner is none.
Whether the file named by sshd's Banner has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue announces the distribution or release (an issue escape or the distro name).
Permission bits of /etc/issue; 0 when the file is absent.
Whether /etc/issue.net has non-whitespace content.
Whether /etc/issue.net announces the distribution or release (an issue escape or the distro name).
Permission bits of /etc/issue.net; 0 when the file is absent.
Whether /etc/motd has non-whitespace content.
Permission bits of /etc/motd; 0 when the file is absent.
Inventory of /etc/update-motd.d entries - name and whether each is executable.
Whether /etc/update-motd.d holds at least one executable script.
Presence and permission facts of /etc/securetty (absent on RHEL 8+ and Debian-family).
Non-comment lines of /etc/securetty. A sibling leaf, not a member of files.etc_securetty, because every leaf under facts is an envelope of its own.
Permission bits of /etc/passwd as an integer (e.g. 420 for 0644).
Owner uid of /etc/passwd.
Group gid of /etc/passwd.
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/passwd.
Group name for the gid of /etc/passwd from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/passwd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/passwd include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/passwd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/passwd include write (derived from mode).
Access ACL entries of /etc/passwd in setfacl form with numeric ids (user::rw-, user:1000:rw-, group::r--, mask::rw-, other::r--); empty when no ACL is set.
Permission bits of /etc/shadow as an integer (e.g. 256 for 0400).
Owner uid of /etc/shadow.
Group gid of /etc/shadow.
Group name for the gid of /etc/shadow from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/shadow include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/shadow include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/shadow include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/shadow include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/shadow.
Access ACL entries of /etc/shadow in setfacl form with numeric ids (user::rw-, user:1000:rw-, group::r--, mask::rw-, other::r--); empty when no ACL is set.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.
Group gid of /etc/hosts.
Group name for the gid of /etc/hosts from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/hosts.
Permission bits of /etc/services as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/services.
Group gid of /etc/services.
Group name for the gid of /etc/services from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/services include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/services include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/services include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/services include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/services.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.lpd.
Group gid of /etc/hosts.lpd.
Group name for the gid of /etc/hosts.lpd from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/hosts.lpd include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/hosts.lpd.
One row per /etc/passwd account with its home path, interactive flag, and the home's stat status, mode, ownership match, group/other write bits and whether it sits on a remote filesystem.
System-scope and per-home shell environment files that exist, with path, scope, owning account, mode, owner match, group/other write bits and whether the file is a symlink.
.rhosts and .shosts files under interactive homes, as derived flags only - owning account match, whether a wildcard "+" entry is present and the non-comment entry count, never the file body.
Permission bits of /root as an integer (e.g. 448 for 0700).
Owner uid of /root.
Group gid of /root.
Whether the group permission bits of /root include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /root include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /root.
Permission bits of /etc/hosts.equiv as an integer; absent when the file does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/hosts.equiv; absent when the file does not exist.
Non-comment lines of /etc/hosts.equiv; an OK empty list when the file does not exist, since a host-based trust file that is absent grants no trust.
Every node one and two levels under /dev, each with name, path, kind, serving filesystem type, mode and owner uid; bounded and marked truncated if the bound is hit.
The subset of /dev entries that are regular files served by the /dev mount itself (not a deeper tmpfs such as /dev/shm) - the stale or planted files U-26 flags.
SysV init scripts and systemd unit files under the startup roots, each with path, mode, owner, group, the group/other-writable flags and is_symlink - the enabled-unit symlinks U-17 filters out.
The startup-script directories themselves (/etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, the rcN.d dirs), each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
The rsyslog and syslog-ng configuration files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
The systemd-journald configuration files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags.
Mode bits of /etc/inetd.conf (0o7777); absent when the file does not exist, as it does not on either stock family.
Owner uid of /etc/inetd.conf; absent when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/inetd.conf is group-writable; absent when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/inetd.conf is world-readable; absent when the file does not exist.
Mode bits of /etc/xinetd.conf (0o7777); absent when the file does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/xinetd.conf; absent when the file does not exist.
The /etc/xinetd.d fragment files, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags; an ok empty list when the directory holds none.
Mode bits of /etc/sudoers (0o7777); absent when the file does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/sudoers; absent when the file does not exist.
Owner gid of /etc/sudoers; absent when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/sudoers carries a POSIX access ACL; denied on a non-root run, since the ACL probe needs the file open.
Mode bits of the /etc/sudoers.d drop-in directory (0o7777); absent when it does not exist.
Owner uid of /etc/sudoers.d; absent when the directory does not exist.
Owner gid of /etc/sudoers.d; absent when the directory does not exist.
Whether /etc/sudoers.d carries a POSIX access ACL; denied on a non-root run, since the ACL probe needs the directory open.
The /etc/sudoers.d drop-in files, each with path, mode, owner, group, the group/other-writable flags and an ignored flag (a name ending in ~ or containing a dot, which sudo skips).
/var/log itself and the directories one and two levels under it, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags; bounded and marked truncated if the bound is hit.

The non-directory entries one and two levels under /var/log, each with path, mode, owner, group and the group/other-writable flags; a symlink is is_symlink:true and an unreadable entry carries a reason. Bounded and marked truncated if the bound is hit.
Non-comment lines of /etc/hosts.allow; an OK empty list when the file does not exist.
Non-comment lines of /etc/hosts.deny; an OK empty list when the file does not exist.
Whether /etc/hosts.deny contains an "ALL:ALL" daemon-to-client deny rule; an OK false when the file does not exist, since a host with no tcp_wrappers deny file is not restricted by it.
Whether /etc/sudoers exists (sudo is configured on the host).
The directory named by the @includedir/#includedir directive in /etc/sudoers; an empty string when none is present.
The Defaults secure_path value from /etc/sudoers (quotes and surrounding spaces stripped); an empty string when unset.
PASS_MAX_DAYS - persisted in login.defs, effective as the maximum over existing accounts' shadow fields.
PASS_MIN_DAYS - persisted in login.defs, effective as the minimum over existing accounts' shadow fields.
PASS_MIN_LEN from login.defs (ignored by PAM when pwquality is present; stage 2 adds the pwquality side).
PASS_WARN_AGE - persisted in login.defs, effective as the minimum warn field over existing accounts' shadow rows.
UID_MIN from login.defs, the lowest uid of a regular (non-system) account.
SYS_UID_MAX from login.defs, the highest uid useradd assigns to a system account.
SHA_CRYPT_MIN_ROUNDS from login.defs.
UMASK from login.defs, verbatim (a mask, not a number).
HOME_MODE from login.defs, verbatim.
ENCRYPT_METHOD from login.defs, verbatim (SHA512, YESCRYPT, ...); PAM may override it.
ENV_SUPATH from login.defs, verbatim (the PATH= assignment for root logins).
ENV_PATH from login.defs, verbatim (the PATH= assignment for other logins).

Local accounts in /etc/passwd order with name, uid, gid, home, shell, system (0 < uid < UID_MIN, where UID_MIN is login.defs' value or 1000 when it is unset or unreadable; nobody is not a system account), shadowed (passwd field is x), uid_duplicate, name_duplicate, shell_valid (shell listed in /etc/shells) and, when /etc/shadow was read or does not exist, password_status (hashed | locked | nopass | noshadow), locked, hash_algo ("$6$"-style id, "legacy" for a hash without one, "" when there is no hash) and the ageing fields; no hashes. Ageing fields are -1 when the shadow field is empty, and uid/gid are -1 when the passwd field is unparsable.

The login shells listed in /etc/shells, in file order; when the file does not exist, the libc default (/bin/sh, /bin/csh) with a reason saying so; carries the read's status when the file is unreadable.
Lines of /etc/passwd and /etc/group that could not be parsed as an account or group (too few fields, a non-numeric uid or gid); a mangled file must not read as a clean host.
Local groups in /etc/group order with name, gid, members (the listed secondary members, duplicates removed), member_count and gid_duplicate.

Accounts whose primary gid names no group in /etc/group, as name and gid in /etc/passwd order; [] when every primary group exists; carries the read's status when /etc/passwd or /etc/group is unreadable.

Members of the administrative groups root, wheel, sudo and admin other than the root account itself - name, group and via (primary when the account's gid is the group's, secondary when listed in /etc/group) - in /etc/group order, primary members before secondary ones.

Whether /etc/shadow exists and every /etc/passwd entry defers to it (password field x); a false names the first account that does not; carries the read's status when /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd is unreadable.
The sources on the passwd line of /etc/nsswitch.conf, in order, with bracketed actions removed; absent when the file or the line is missing (glibc then resolves from files).
The sources on the group line of /etc/nsswitch.conf, in order, with bracketed actions removed; absent when the file or the line is missing.

Whether the passwd or group database names a remote source in use: any source other than files, compat, systemd or db, where sss counts only when /etc/sssd/sssd.conf exists (compat's NIS + entries are not detected); account controls judged on the local files report WARN while this is true (spec section 7.3).

The expanded PAM stacks of login, sshd, su, sudo, passwd and other (those whose /etc/pam.d file exists) - service, type, control, module, args, path, line - with @include, include and substack spliced where they stand and authselect's symlinks resolved by name into /etc/authselect, never by following the link. Backslash line continuation and a pam.conf-only host are not handled.
How the stacks are generated - authselect (a managed file is a symlink into /etc/authselect), pam-auth-update (the marker in common-auth) or manual.

Whether every include of every published service was read; a false names the first unreadable, missing, undeclared, looping or too-deep include in its reason, and every derived pam.* value then carries error instead of a number.
pam_pwquality.so is stacked in passwd's password stack with a control field other than optional; a false names why. Every other pam.pwquality.* key is absent while this is false.
The local_users_only argument or setting is present, so pwquality skips accounts that are not in /etc/passwd.
Effective minlen - the default 8, then pwquality.conf, then pwquality.conf.d/*.conf in name order, then the module arguments, each overriding the last.
Effective minclass (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective dcredit (default 0), resolved like minlen; a negative value is a minimum count of digits.
Effective ucredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective lcredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
Effective ocredit (default 0), resolved like minlen.
The character classes a new password must contain - the larger of minclass and the number of credits set to -1 or lower.
enforce_for_root is set in a conf file or as a module argument.

The hashing argument on pam_unix.so in passwd's password stack (md5, bigcrypt, sha256, sha512, blowfish, gost_yescrypt or yescrypt); empty when none is given and login.defs ENCRYPT_METHOD decides; absent when the stack has no pam_unix line.

How many previous passwords a new one is checked against - remember= on pam_pwhistory.so (argument, else pwhistory.conf, else the module default 10) or on pam_unix.so; absent when neither module sets it.

Every existing login-facing service (login, sshd) stacks pam_faillock.so with preauth and with authfail in its auth phase and, in its account phase, pam_faillock.so, or an authsucc line in the auth phase; a false names the first service that does not. The other pam.faillock.* keys are absent while this is false.

Effective deny - the default 3, then faillock.conf, then the preauth arguments, then the authfail arguments; 0 disables the lockout. What is published is the merge of faillock.conf, the preauth arguments and the authfail arguments, the authfail line applied last; when the two lines disagree pam.faillock.enabled says so in its reason. A conf= argument naming another file is not handled.
Effective unlock_time in seconds (default 600), resolved like deny; 0 means the account stays locked until an administrator releases it.
Effective fail_interval in seconds (default 900), resolved like deny.
even_deny_root is set in faillock.conf or as a module argument (with or without a value), or root_unlock_time is set, which implies it.
Effective root_unlock_time in seconds, resolved like deny; unlock_time when not set.
su's auth stack has a pam_wheel.so line whose control field is required or requisite and whose arguments do not include deny, so only the wheel group (or group=) may use su; a false names why.
The control field of the first pam_wheel.so line in su's auth stack; absent when there is none.
The group pam_wheel.so restricts su to - its group= argument, or wheel; absent when there is no pam_wheel line.
The arguments of that pam_wheel.so line; absent when there is none.
pam_umask.so is in the session stack of login (else sshd, else other), which applies a umask where /etc/profile never runs.
The arguments of the first pam_umask.so session line; absent when the module is not stacked.
login's auth stack has a pam_securetty.so line (any control), so /etc/securetty is consulted for root logins on a console; absent when there is no login service.
Container runtime detected from filesystem markers (none, docker, podman, lxc, other); the same value the run header carries.
Whether /run/systemd/system exists, so unit state can be asked of systemd.
Effective TMOUT in seconds from the system profile files; 0 when unset (bash reads 0 as no timeout).
Whether the winning TMOUT is exported so child login shells inherit it.
Whether TMOUT is made readonly so a user cannot unset it.
Every TMOUT assignment - path, line, value, exported, readonly, conditional, scope.
Every umask assignment - path, line, value, symbolic, conditional, scope.
The winning PATH assignment for root, verbatim, with its file and line.
Each root PATH element - position, value, exists, mode, uid, gid, group_writable, world_writable, is_dot, variable, unresolved, undeclared.
World-writable files found by the deep walk, with path, sticky, uid, gid, package_declared.
Whether the deep walk finished within its budget.
Every cron/at configuration and spool file - path, scope, user, mode, owner and the group/other-writable flags.
The cron and at directories - path, mode, owner and the group/other-writable flags.
The systemd timer unit-file inventory - name and enablement state.
The detected firewall backend (firewalld, ufw, nftables, iptables or none); unsupported/denied when the kernel ruleset could not be read.
Whether a host firewall is on - runtime from a non-empty kernel ruleset, persisted from the backend configuration on disk.
The default policy of the INPUT hook (accept/drop) - runtime from the base-chain policy, persisted from the backend configuration.
The default policy of the FORWARD hook (accept/drop) - runtime from the base-chain policy, persisted from the backend configuration.

Whether the ruleset restricts inbound traffic by default (derived by normalisation); absent when confidence is below full (accept-with-rules, mixed policies, a missing policy, a non-input inbound chain with rules, or a truncated dump); the unsupported/denied envelope when the ruleset could not be read.

Confidence in the normalised inbound judgement - full (every input filter chain is drop/reject, or every input filter chain is accept with zero rules) or partial (everything else - accept-with-rules, mixed policies, a missing policy, a non-input inbound chain with rules, or a truncated dump); the unsupported/denied envelope when the ruleset could not be read.

The normalised inbound-affecting rules, each with chain, action, protocol, dport (a string, since ports may be ranges or sets) and source; the unsupported/denied envelope when the ruleset could not be read.
The captured kernel ruleset dumps, each with source (the command), content (capped at 64 KiB) and truncated; the raw evidence the normaliser parses.

Which time-synchronisation provider is configured on disk - chrony, timesyncd, ntpd or none; chosen from the persisted configuration in the order chrony, ntpd, systemd-timesyncd, so a leftover configuration file of a removed provider still decides and should be purged. Evidence only (which daemon is running is services.ntp.active).

The de-duplicated, sorted time sources the provider is configured with - server/pool/peer names, chrony reference clocks as refclock:<driver>:<arg>, and (timesyncd) the lists timedatectl show-timesync reports; absent when the effective list cannot be known (timedatectl unavailable on the timesyncd branch, or a chrony sourcedir/confdir outside the collector's declaration).
How many time sources time_sync.servers holds; 0 when no provider is configured, and absent under the same conditions as time_sync.servers.

Whether the host's clock is currently synchronised, from timedatectl NTPSynchronized; evidence only (a freshly booted or air-gapped host is not a finding), and unsupported wherever timedatectl cannot run.

Which syslog implementation is configured on disk - rsyslog, syslog-ng, journald-only or none; a daemon is named only when its binary is installed as well as its configuration file, so a conffile left behind by a removed package does not decide. Evidence only (which daemon is running is services.syslog.active).

The rsyslog routing rules in file order, one record per selected facility and action, each with facility, priority, target and target_kind (file, device, remote, user, pipe, program, module or discard; a device is a /dev/ target, which is logged but keeps nothing); absent when the host has no rsyslog configuration, and the read's status when a configuration file exists but cannot be read.

Whether every rsyslog configuration file the main file includes was read; false when an include could not be read or named a path outside the collector's declaration, which makes logging.rsyslog.coverage absent.

How many rsyslog constructs this version does not model - an if/then conditional, a ruleset() or call statement (and the legacy $RuleSet/$DefaultRuleset), an action that runs only when the previous one was suspended or only every Nth message, a property filter on the facility or severity, a discard restricted to some severities, a numeric facility or priority code, a ?TemplateName dynamic file target, and an omfile or omfwd action whose argument cannot be parsed; any of them makes logging.rsyslog.coverage absent.

How many property-based filter lines the configuration carries (the leading-colon msg/syslogtag form); they add a destination for a tagged subset of messages and can never un-log a facility, so they are evidence only and leave coverage untouched; a filter on the facility or severity property is counted in logging.rsyslog.unmodelled instead, since it can.

Per-facility routing derived from the rules in file order, each with facility, logged, priority_floor, target, persistent and reason; persistent means the winning target is a local file path, not that the file already exists - a remote collector and a /dev/ device are logged but never persistent. Absent when the parse was incomplete, when an unmodelled construct was seen, or when the host has no rsyslog configuration.

journald's Storage= from /etc/systemd/journald.conf (or the /usr/lib copy) merged with its drop-in directories - persisted as configured (auto when unset, journald's default), runtime as persistent or volatile from whether /var/log/journal is a directory; the read's status on both sides when a file in the chain exists but cannot be read, and unsupported on a host with no systemd.
journald's merged ForwardToSyslog=, false when unset (journald's default); evidence only, since forwarding neither adds nor removes journal storage.

Whether the journal survives a reboot - true when Storage is persistent, or when it is auto (the default, and what journald falls back to for a value it cannot parse) and /var/log/journal is a directory; the read's status when a configuration file in the chain exists but cannot be read, and unsupported on a host with no systemd.

The distinct local file targets the rules name, each with path, exists, persistent, mtime_age_s and stat_status (ok, absent, denied, error or undeclared); mtime_age_s is the whole seconds between the file's modification time and the run's collected_at and is omitted when either is unknown or the file was modified after the run started, and a path outside the collector's declaration is recorded with stat_status undeclared and never stat-ed. Evidence only.

Every NFS export as {path, client, options, wildcard, root_squash} parsed from /etc/exports and /etc/exports.d/*.exports; a path with no client spec, or a bare "(options)" spec with a space before the parenthesis (exportfs's own space-sensitive trap), exports to the world (client "*", wildcard true); root_squash is derived from the absence of no_root_squash in the client's options.
The export files actually read, in the order they were parsed.
Whether exportfs -v ran successfully to corroborate the parsed exports; exportfs is never the judged source, so its absence or a non-root failure is recorded as false, never an error.
Permission bits of /etc/exports as an integer (e.g. 384 for 0600).
Owner uid of /etc/exports.
Group gid of /etc/exports.
Group name for the gid of /etc/exports from /etc/group; empty when the gid has no name.
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/exports include read (derived from mode).
Whether the group permission bits of /etc/exports include write (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/exports include read (derived from mode).
Whether the other permission bits of /etc/exports include write (derived from mode).
Whether a POSIX ACL xattr is present on /etc/exports.

The SNMP protocol versions the configuration enables, a subset of v1, v2c and v3; a rocommunity/rwcommunity directive enables both v1 and v2c, a com2sec enables a version only once a group names that model for its security name, and v3 is enabled by the existence of any v3 user. Absent when no snmpd configuration was found, or when part of it could not be read.

Every configured SNMP community, REDACTED to {ref, kind, is_default, length, source_restricted} - the string itself is never stored, not even hashed, since a hash of a short well-known word is trivially reversible. ref is an opaque ordinal (c1, c2, ...) in file order; kind is ro, rw, trap or proxy (a com2sec community is rw only when an access rule reachable from its security name grants a write view; trap is a trapcommunity, a community named by a trapsink, trap2sink, informsink or by a trapsess -c option, or - for a trap destination that names none and has no trapcommunity directive above it - net-snmp's compiled-in fallback, which is recorded once per such destination because the agent really does send it; proxy is the community a proxy directive forwards with, read from its -c option, with the destination host and the OID subtree never stored; trap and proxy are both outbound and carry no source); is_default says the string is one of the collector's embedded well-known defaults; length is its rune count; and source_restricted says it is bound to a source other than default or an any-address form.

The SNMPv3 users named by a createUser, rouser or rwuser directive, as {name, auth_proto, priv_proto, level} sorted by name; a usmUser line in the persistent state file is not parsed, so a user with no createUser and no rouser/rwuser is not listed. No passphrase, master key or localized key is ever stored - auth_proto and priv_proto are filled only from an allow-list of protocol names and are empty for a user whose protocols were not named. level is the level the user's key material supports, falling back to the minimum an access line demands. Absent when no snmpd configuration was found, or when part of it could not be read.

The VACM and community-mapping lines in file order as {kind, name, sec_model, sec_level, source, read_view, write_view}; kind is com2sec, group, view or access. Each kind fills the fields that carry its meaning - com2sec puts the security name in name and the address or range in source; group puts the group name in name, the model in sec_model and the security name in source; view puts the view name in name, included/excluded in sec_level and the OID subtree in source; access puts the group name in name, the context in source and the two views in read_view/write_view. A com2sec community string is never one of the fields.
The listen specifications of every agentaddress directive in file order, one entry per comma-separated spec.

The snmpd configuration files actually read, sorted; includes followed through includeFile and includeDir appear alongside the declared candidates, and each file appears exactly once however it was reached.

Whether every configuration file the collector was told to read could be read; false when a read failed or when an includeFile/includeDir named a target outside the collector's declaration, which is recorded and never touched. A host with no snmpd configuration at all read everything there was, so the parse is complete and the judged lists carry that story instead.

The package manager this host is judged through - apt when the dpkg database exists, dnf when the dnf metadata cache directory does, otherwise unknown, in which case every other patch fact is unsupported.

Whole seconds between the newest cached package metadata (the newest apt Packages list or update-success stamp; the newest dnf repomd.xml) and the run's collected_at, so the same snapshot always renders the same age. A cache NEWER than collected_at - an index rewritten between the run's single clock reading and this stat, or a little clock skew - is a cache refreshed during the run, so the age is floored at zero and the reason says why; it is never reported as underivable, which would hide the pending security count under a not-applicable result. Absent when the host holds no metadata cache at all, and then pending_security_count is absent too; muster never refreshes the metadata itself.

Whether the metadata cache carries a security channel at all - an apt list file of a -security suite, or a cached repomd.xml declaring an updateinfo data section. It is decided from the cached files, never from a command's exit code, because a security query that exits cleanly with no output says the same thing whether the channel is missing or nothing is pending. A cached repomd that exists but cannot be READ carries that read's status here - denied on an unprivileged run - rather than a false, so an unreadable cache is never reported as a host with no security channel.

How many pending updates come from a security channel - counted from the origins of the cache-only apt simulation, and from the cached updateinfo on dnf. Unsupported when a cache exists but carries no security channel, never 0, which would read as nothing pending; absent when there is no metadata cache at all.

The upgrades the cache-only simulation reports as {name, current, candidate, origin}, sorted by name then candidate; current is empty for a package the upgrade would newly install, and origin is the suite or repository the candidate comes from. Evidence only, and never obtained by refreshing metadata.

Whether the host is waiting for a reboot - the /run/reboot-required flag on apt hosts, needs-restarting -r on dnf hosts. Unsupported inside a container, where the kernel belongs to the host rather than to this namespace and nothing is run at all, and unsupported where needs-restarting, which the dnf-utils package ships, is not installed.

Whether unattended upgrades are configured to apply updates - persisted from APT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade or from dnf-automatic's apply_updates. The runtime side is not probed in this version, since a timer's state belongs to the services inventory. Evidence only - a fleet may patch centrally by policy.
Packages pinned to their current version and therefore held back from an upgrade, sorted; from apt-mark showhold. Unsupported on dnf hosts, whose versionlock plugin is not probed in this version.

Whole days between the newest package installation the dpkg log records and the run's collected_at. dpkg writes local time with no zone and collected_at is UTC, so this is a whole-day approximation that can be one day out on a host away from UTC - evidence that a host is being maintained, never a judged value. Absent when the log records no installation, and unsupported on dnf hosts, whose rpm installation times are not probed in this version.
Installed packages as {name, version, arch} read from the package database (dpkg status on apt hosts, rpm -qa on dnf hosts); a version is evidence only and is never obtained by invoking a daemon.
